text:
sam: Heads-up — onprem-prod reported unexpected outbound KMS traffic to 54.23.12.9 right after I applied the RBAC tweak to service-account policy. Not sure if it's misconfig or compromised token. Anyone on call?

ops-bot: [ALERT] egress-anomaly detected for cluster priv-prod at 2026-03-22T17:42Z. 78 requests to 54.23.12.9 (kms.example) from svc acc:redwood-infer-svc. Actions: flagged, rate-limited.

anita: @sam can you paste the exact kubectl patch you applied? also need pod list and SA last-used. quick commands:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --show-labels
kubectl get rolebinding -n inference -o yaml | grep -C3 redwood-infer-svc
kubectl auth can-i create secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:inference:redwood-infer-svc
```

sam: patched with a narrow rolebinding (removed edit->create secrets) at 17:40:12 UTC. attaching logs of the patch command output below.

sam: ```
kubectl patch rolebinding inference-sa-binding -n inference --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/subjects/0/roleRef","value":{"name":"inference-read"}}]'
```

dinesh: I'm seeing the same IP in VPC flow logs — egress via NAT-gw-3 at 17:41:05. Likely one pod started replaying cached requests. Can someone run `kubectl exec` into the suspect pod and check /proc/1/environ and mounted tokens?

clare: Oncall here. Running `kubectl top pod` to find CPU spikes. Also suggest we revoke SA tokens and redeploy pod as quick containment: rotate secret, force restart.

maria: Agree containment first. Proposed steps:
1) create scoped temp SA with no egress perms
2) patch workload to use temp SA
3) rotate KMS key access policy to deny 54.23.12.9 if external
4) collect audit logs: kube-apiserver, kubelet, and our audit proxy

jen: I'll run the ephemeral rotation. Command I'm about to run:
```
# rotate token
kubectl delete secret -n inference sa-redwood-infer-token
kubectl rollout restart deploy inference-worker -n inference
```

anita: Also ensure audit logs include the RBAC change event — check kube-audit logs and our control-plane audit stream. If there's unusual `impersonate` calls, escalate.

dinesh: I've pulled the audit lines. No impersonate but there are repeated successful GETs to /v1/decrypt from the pod using the SA token after the patch. копия of log snippet:
```
"user":{"username":"system:serviceaccount:inference:redwood-infer-svc"}, "verb":"get","resource":"decrypt" ,"timestamp":"2026-03-22T17:41:06Z"
```

sam: Thanks. Sounds like the SA had access and a pod started retrying. Next steps: full token rotation, revoke any long-lived creds, run offline scan of container images for leaked creds, and open a vuln-triage ticket.

maria: I'll own vuln-triage ticket and coordinate customer notification if data plane KMS keys were used externally. tagging @legal if needed. :shield:

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-324 — onprem egress KMS anomaly. Assignees: anita, dinesh, jen. Priority: P2.

clare: I'll update runbook with a quick checklist for RBAC-change rollback + telemetry probes so this doesn't recur. Short term mitigation applied, will follow up with postmortem notes.

sam: appreciate the quick responses. Will keep this thread updated with artifact links and timelines.
